place.printed: the immediate right of the First Corps, north of the town

source.author: Lieut. Col. Adolphus Dobke

place.printed: the cemetery behind the stone fence

place.printed: the stone fence in the woods on the right (Twelfth Corps front); returned to Cemetery Hill at 2.30 a. m.

source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R256 Lieut. Col. Adolphus Dobke, p. 735

place.printed: Cemetery Hill

activity: The most vehement artillery cross-fire had to be sustained from 12 m. to 4 p. m. July 3, and particularly from 2 to 4 p. m.

source.author: Lieut. Col. Adolphus Dobke
source.quote: vehement artillery cross-fire had to be sustained from 12 m. to 4 p. m.
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R256 Lieut. Col. Adolphus Dobke, p. 736

note: Also has fire since 3.45 a. m. against the right wing.

place.printed: Gettysburg

place.printed: the cemetery south of Gettysburg, behind breastworks

source.author: Lieut. Col. William H. H. Bown
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R258 Lieut. Col. William H. H. Bown, p. 738

note: Earthwork evidence: "breastworks" at the cemetery.

place.printed: the Twelfth Corps front on the right

activity: In the evening of July 2 the 61st Ohio and 157th NY under Colonel McGroarty were sent to support the Twelfth Corps, were repulsed and returned to the old position

source.author: Lieut. Col. William H. H. Bown
source.quote: were sent to support the Twelfth Corps
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R258 Lieut. Col. William H. H. Bown, p. 738

note: Gazetteer ref by inference.

when.printed: the night from June 30 to July 1

place.printed: Creagerstown direction, about 5 miles

activity: Captain Koenig with 100 men made a reconnaissance toward Creagerstown in the night of June 30 to July 1; returned to the Emmitsburg camp about 9 a. m., followed the corps and arrived at Gettysburg about 3.30 p. m.

when.printed: late in the evening of July 1

place.printed: behind a stone fence in front of Cemetery Hill

activity: Late evening July 1 the detachment rejoined the brigade, stationed behind a stone fence in front of Cemetery Hill in two lines (second line)

source.author: Capt. Emil Koenig
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R259 Capt. Emil Koenig, p. 740
source.extract: which was stationed behind a stone fence in front of Cemetery Hill

place.printed: to the right toward Wiedrich's battery

activity: About 8 p. m. July 2 the regiment ordered ahead and to the left of the brigade, then suddenly to the right toward Wiedrich's battery, relieved by the 41st NY, returned to its original position

source.author: Capt. Emil Koenig
source.quote: our regiment was ordered ahead and to the left of the brigade
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R259 Capt. Emil Koenig, p. 740

place.printed: behind a stone fence to the left of Wiedrich's battery, right of the road to Gettysburg

activity: At 6 o'clock on the morning of July 3 ordered to the right of the road leading to Gettysburg, posted behind a stone fence to the left of Wiedrich's battery; one company in the next houses of the town

source.author: Capt. Emil Koenig
source.quote: We were posted behind a stone fence to the left of Captain

note: Road not named (Baltimore Pike by position).

place.printed: Gettysburg (11 miles from the start)

source.author: Maj. Benjamin A. Willis

note: "Chambersburg road" as printed in this report for the road north-west of town (Carlisle/Mummasburg directions not named).

when.printed: About 4 p. m.; about 9 p. m.

place.printed: the cemetery position; the battery on East Cemetery Hill

activity: About 4 p. m. July 2 opened what is said to be the grandest cannonade of the war, lasting about five hours; about 9 p. m. the 119th and 58th New York led by Krzyzanowski charged to save the battery

source.author: Maj. Benjamin A. Willis
source.quote: About 4 p. m. opened what is said to be the grandest cannonade
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R260 Maj. Benjamin A. Willis, p. 743

note: Willis puts the night charge at about 9 p. m.

place.printed: a field opposite the cemetery

activity: During the night of July 2 the regiment took position opposite the cemetery in a field and remained during July 3

source.author: Maj. Benjamin A. Willis
source.quote: to take position opposite the cemetery, in a field
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R260 Maj. Benjamin A. Willis, p. 743

note: Covers July 3. Note: Willis dates the cannonade of July 3 with blanks ("from — a. m. until — p. m.").

place.printed: easterly toward York, about 2 miles

activity: About 8 a. m. July 4 the 119th NY and 26th Wisconsin made a reconnaissance in an easterly direction toward York for about 2 miles, taking many prisoners, then returned

source.author: Maj. Benjamin A. Willis
source.quote: in an easterly direction toward York for the distance of about 2 miles
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R260 Maj. Benjamin A. Willis, p. 743

place.printed: west of and near the cemetery building

source.author: Lieut. Col. David Thomson
source.quote: I placed the regiment west of and near that building
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R261 Lieut. Col. David Thomson, p. 744

note: "That building" = the cemetery building (gatehouse) per the preceding sentence.

place.printed: camp at Emmitsburg

activity: 75th Pennsylvania left camp at 5 a. m. July 1 and proceeded to Gettysburg

place.printed: the north side of the town

place.printed: north of the town, a wheat-field half a mile out

source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R262 Maj. August Ledig, p. 745

place.printed: a corn-field behind a stone wall below the Evergreen Cemetery

source.author: Maj. August Ledig
source.quote: behind a stone wall, below the Evergreen Cemetery
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R262 Maj. August Ledig, p. 745

note: Cemetery unspecified wall; Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse used as the nearest gazetteer anchor.

place.printed: the village of Gettysburg; the extreme right of the brigade

source.author: Col. William H. Jacobs
source.quote: the regiment arrived with the rest of your command
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R263 Col. William H. Jacobs, p. 746

place.printed: Cemetery Hill, behind the stone fence

source.author: Col. William H. Jacobs

source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R263 Col. William H. Jacobs, p. 746

source.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R264 Maj. Thomas W. Osbom, p. 747
source.extract: After moving 5 or 6 miles, I received notice from Major-General Howard

place.printed: the front of and 300 yards beyond the town

place.printed: about three-fourths of a mile from the town on the left of the York pike

source.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
source.quote: About 11 a. m. Lieutenant Wilkeson reached the field
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R264 Maj. Thomas W. Osbom, p. 748

note: Wilkeson was mortally wounded at almost the first fire.

place.printed: the hill immediately in front of the cemetery entrance, overlooking the town

source.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
source.quote: to a position on the hill immediately in front of the cemetery entrance
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R264 Maj. Thomas W. Osbom, p. 748

note: Wainwright took command of this battery with the artillery on that side of the Baltimore pike on the afternoon of the 1st (Osborn).

place.printed: the town, then the rear

activity: Heckman was ordered in only when the corps began to fall back; one gun lost; the battery was sent to the rear and took no part on July 2-3

source.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R264 Maj. Thomas W. Osbom, p. 748
source.extract: Captain Heckman was not ordered in until the corps had begun to fall back

when.printed: the morning of July 3 (same as July 2)

place.printed: Cemetery Hill, Dilger on the right next to the Baltimore road

source.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
source.quote: had the right, resting next the Baltimore road and parallel with the Emmitsburg road
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R264 Maj. Thomas W. Osbom, p. 749

when.printed: between 7 and 8 o'clock in the evening

source.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
source.quote: 7 and 8 o'clock in the evening, a rebel brigade charged from the town
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R264 Maj. Thomas W. Osbom, p. 749

note: t_iso is the start of the printed range 7-8.

place.printed: Cemetery Hill

activity: About 3 p. m. July 3 the enemy opened along the whole front with an unbroken line of artillery and heavily on the right flank

source.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom

place.printed: the hill on the north side of the Baltimore turnpike

source.author: Capt. Michael Wiedrich

note: Howard: columns reached Cemetery Hill 4.30.

place.printed: the battery on the hill east of the cemetery

source.author: Capt. Michael Wiedrich
source.quote: the enemy charged on the battery with a brigade of infantry
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R265 Capt. Michael Wiedrich, p. 752

place.printed: the hill east of the cemetery

source.author: Capt. Michael Wiedrich
source.quote: until about 1 p. m., when the battle became general
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R265 Capt. Michael Wiedrich, p. 752

note: Agrees with Howard's about 1 p. m.; Osborn says about 3 p. m.

place.printed: Emmitsburg; within about 5 miles of Gettysburg

place.printed: the front north of the town, on Dilger's right

source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R266 Lieut. William Wheeler, p. 752

place.printed: Cemetery Hill, left wing of the batteries

source.author: Lieut. William Wheeler
source.quote: being on the left wing of the batteries of the corps
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R266 Lieut. William Wheeler, p. 753

place.printed: Cemetery Hill

activity: At about 2 p. m. (printed; other reports say about 4) the rebel batteries opened along the front and on the right flank; at about 5.30 p. m. ammunition exhausted and another battery sent to relieve

source.quote: At about 2 p. m. the rebel batteries opened along our front
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R266 Lieut. William Wheeler, p. 753

note: July 2 start of the bombardment is about 4 p. m. in Wainwright, Hall, Breck, Cooper, Steinwehr, Schurz, Howard. The digit may be OCR; recorded as printed.

place.printed: behind Cemetery Hill

activity: During the cannonade from 1 to 3 p. m. July 3 the battery lay in reserve behind Cemetery Hill and lost some horses

source.author: Lieut. William Wheeler
source.quote: During the heavy cannonade from 1 to 3 p. m.
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R266 Lieut. William Wheeler, p. 753

note: t_iso is the start of the printed range 1-3.

place.printed: the Second Corps front, on the left of Pettit's battery, enemy about 400 yards off

place.printed: Gettysburg; position "between the Taneytown and Baltimore road"

source.quote: The battery arrived at Gettysburg at about 10 a. m. July 1

place.printed: 600 yards on the right on the Baltimore and Harrisburg road

source.author: Capt. Hubert DUger
source.quote: about 600 yards on our right, on the Baltimore and Harrisburg road
source.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R267 Capt. Hubert DUger, p. 754

place.printed: around the town to Cemetery Hill

place.printed: the east side of the town

place.printed: the rear

place.printed: camp near Emmitsburg

place.printed: the north side of the York road, some distance eastward of the poor-house

source.author: Lieut. Eugene A. Bancroft

source.author: Lieut. Eugene A. Bancroft
